de.title: Das Faltpapier
de.instruction: Malt auf dem Papier. Legt die Faltlinie dahin, wo ihr den Spiegel vermutet. Faltet und schaut nach.
de.tryElsewhere: Legt die Faltlinie jetzt woanders hin.
de.hangsOff: Ein Stück schaut über den Rand hinaus.
de.emptyNote: Malt ein paar Kästchen aus und faltet dann.
de._notes: REJECTED 'Faltblatt' (the builder draft) — a Faltblatt is a folded LEAFLET; the whole panel read it as advertising. 'Faltpapier' is the craft-cupboard material word. REJECTED 'Falz' (bookbinding/plumbing jargon) and 'Knick' (names damage left AFTER folding); 'Faltlinie' is on every Grundschule worksheet. Symmetrieachse never used — Klasse 4, and naming the axis is exactly what this tool withholds. 'Kästchen' because the paper is Kästchenpapier. Class-plural imperative throughout: a teacher speaks over this at the board.

nl.title: Het vouwblad
nl.instruction: Kleur op het blad. Leg de vouw waar je denkt dat de spiegel zit. Vouw het en kijk.
nl.tryElsewhere: Leg de vouw nu eens ergens anders.
nl.hangsOff: Een stukje steekt over de rand.
nl.emptyNote: Kleur een paar hokjes en vouw dan.
nl._notes: KEPT 'vouwblad' emphatically: vouwblaadjes are the coloured paper squares every Dutch kleuter folds, so the name already means something in the child's hands. REJECTED 'verven' — in Dutch that is painting a house or a wall; children KLEUREN. REJECTED 'Laat de spiegel zien' — what appears is het spiegelbeeld, not a mirror. symmetrieas/spiegelas rejected outright (groep 6-7, and it hands over the answer the fold is meant to produce). 'Hokjes' over 'ruitjes': ruitjespapier is the paper, hokjes are what you colour in. Register: 'je', not 'jullie' — Dutch board materials for groep 1-4 address the child singular even with the class watching.

sv.title: Vikpappret
sv.instruction: Måla på pappret. Lägg vikningen där ni tror att spegeln finns. Vik och se efter.
sv.tryElsewhere: Prova vikningen på ett annat ställe.
sv.emptyNote: Måla några rutor och vik sedan.
sv._notes: [NSR-FLAG] REJECTED the draft 'Vikbladet' — a coinage; 'vikpapper' is a real material word (the folding paper sold for förskolan), so the title names something the child has held. Considered 'vecket' for the crease but chose 'vikningen': the line is placed BEFORE anything is folded, so it is the fold-to-be, not a mark. Deliberately avoided all -linje/-axel compounds so nothing edges toward symmetrilinje/spegelaxel (åk 4). 'Visa spegelbilden' — it is the image that appears. Kept 'Suddgummi' over the shorter 'sudd': as a lone button 'Sudd' reads as the verb. Least sure about the title and 'på tvären'.

fr.title: La feuille à plier
fr.instruction: Coloriez des carreaux. Placez le pli là où vous pensez que le miroir se trouve. Pliez et regardez.
fr.gatePrint: L’impression fait partie de l’offre Enseignant.
fr._notes: REJECTED 'peignez/peinture' — peindre means gouache, brushes and aprons; a cycle-2 child filling squares COLORIE. REJECTED 'deux couches' — une couche is a nappy and the class will say so; 'deux épaisseurs' is the real paper word. Fixed a register slip in the draft ('Montre-moi' tu inside vous-form copy). Introduced a distinction English cannot make: LE MIROIR is where you would stand the mirror (the instruction keeps it), LE REFLET is what it would show — so the ghost buttons say reflet. 'Axe de symétrie' never appears: CM1 vocabulary, and it names what the fold is meant to reveal.

es.title: La hoja para doblar
es.instruction: Coloreen en la hoja. Pongan el doblez donde creen que está el espejo. Doblen y vean qué pasa.
es.tryElsewhere: Ahora pongan el doblez en otro lugar.
es.hangsOff: Una parte se sale del borde.
es.gatePrint: La impresión es parte del plan Docente.
es.emptyNote: Coloreen algunos cuadritos y luego doblen.
es._notes: Mexican throughout. REJECTED 'pinten/pintura' — pintar is a brush and a bote de pintura; in the salón children COLOREAN los cuadritos. REJECTED 'el pliegue' (technical, closer to a pleat in cloth); 'el doblez' is what a maestra says. REJECTED 'goma' for the eraser — peninsular; in Mexico that is chicle or the material — 'borrador' is the child's word. Kept 'encimados' because encimar is what the paper physically does. Deliberate register split: teacher-voice lines use USTEDES, the mirror button is tú because a child taps it and is talking to the tool. 'Eje de simetría' never appears.

it.title: Il foglio che si piega
it.instruction: Colora sul foglio. Metti la piega dove pensi che ci sia lo specchio. Piega e scopri.
it.tryElsewhere: Ora prova la piega in un altro punto.
it.hangsOff: Un pezzo finisce fuori dal foglio.
it.gatePrint: Stampare il foglio fa parte del piano Insegnante.
it._notes: REJECTED 'asse di simmetria' and every form of simmetrico — classe quarta naming vocabulary; the panel was unanimous that even the adjective would turn the routine into a quiz. REJECTED 'piegatura' as the label — in classe prima it reads as the ACT of folding; 'la piega' is the LINE the child can point to. REJECTED 'cancellino' for the eraser — that is the blackboard duster; 'gomma' is the only word a six-year-old uses. REJECTED 'casella' (a box on a form or board game) — the squared exercise book is the quaderno a quadretti, so 'quadretto' is the classroom word.

pt.title: A folha que dobra
pt.instruction: Pinte na folha. Ponha o vinco onde você acha que está o espelho. Dobre e descubra.
pt.tryElsewhere: Agora experimente o vinco em outro lugar.
pt.creaseH: Vinco de um lado a outro
pt.creaseD: Vinco de um canto a outro
pt.hangsOff: Uma parte fica para fora da folha.
pt.gatePrint: Imprimir a folha faz parte do plano Professor.
pt.emptyNote: Pinte alguns quadradinhos e depois dobre.
pt._notes: Brazilian register throughout (você, quadradinhos, borracha). REJECTED 'eixo de simetria' — fourth-year vocabulary; the teacher on the panel said naming the eixo is exactly what stops the child moving the crease a second time. REJECTED 'dobradura', the obvious first word and wrong: in a Brazilian school dobradura is the paper-craft/origami lesson, a different activity — so the panel split the job the way the tool does, 'dobrar' for the action and 'vinco' for the mark the fold leaves. REJECTED 'quadrícula' (European and technical) for 'quadradinhos'.

da.title: Foldearket
da.instruction: Farvelæg nogle tern på arket. Læg folden der, hvor du tror spejlet er. Fold, og find ud af det.
da.tryElsewhere: Prøv nu folden et andet sted.
da.hangsOff: En del af det hænger ud over kanten.
da.gatePrint: Print af arket hører til Lærerabonnementet.
da.emptyNote: Farvelæg nogle tern, og fold så.
da._notes: [NSR-FLAG] THE IMPORTANT ONE: REJECTED 'Lærerplanen'. En læreplan is the CURRICULUM in Danish schooling — a teacher reading it on a paywall chip parses it as a curriculum document, not a subscription, and the false friend is close enough to mislead. 'Lærerabonnementet' is unambiguous. Also rejected symmetriakse/spejlingsakse (indskolingen genuinely does not use them); 'felter' for the squares (correct but flat — ternet papir is the classroom object); and 'et lag' without the accent — 'ét lag' is written with the accent so it reads as the NUMBER one, or the contrast with 'to lag' goes soft.

no.title: Arket vi bretter
no.instruction: Fargelegg noen ruter på arket. Legg brettelinjen der du tror speilet er. Brett, og se hva som skjer.
no.tryElsewhere: Prøv nå brettelinjen et annet sted.
no.hangsOff: Noe av det havner utenfor arket.
no.gatePrint: Utskrift av arket hører til Lærerabonnementet.
no.emptyNote: Fargelegg noen ruter, og brett så.
no._notes: [NSR-FLAG] Bokmål. REJECTED 'bretten' as the short crease label — the panel's first instinct and a trap: et brett is a TRAY, so 'Legg bretten her' reads as put the tray here. It has to be 'brettelinjen', longer than wanted for a chip but the only unambiguous form; if the row overflows, shorten the surrounding chips, not this one. REJECTED 'folde' (leans toward pleating and written register) — a Norwegian child BRETTER papir. REJECTED 'Lærerplanen', same curriculum collision as Danish. 'ett lag' with double t so it is unmistakably the numeral against 'to lag'. Title 'Arket vi bretter' over the compound because the classroom 'vi' makes it a thing the class does together.

fi.title: Taittuva paperi
fi.instruction: Väritä ruutuja paperiin. Aseta taite sinne, missä uskot peilin olevan. Taita ja katso, mitä tapahtuu.
fi.emptyNote: Väritä muutama ruutu ja taita sitten.
fi._notes: [NSR-FLAG] THE PLACEHOLDER TRAP, HANDLED: cellAria stays in the plain nominative because {r} and {c} arrive as bare cardinals. The ordinal shape the panel wanted first — '{r}. rivi' — is what a Finnish teacher actually says, but it needs the placeholder to supply an ordinal (kolmas, not kolme), and a screen reader would read the number three followed by a full stop. Rejected for that reason alone, and the same principle applied everywhere: no string wraps a placeholder in a case ending. REJECTED 'taitos' for the crease — taitos is the fold you have already MADE; 'taite' is the LINE the child moves before folding, so the whole thesis depends on this word. REJECTED 'kaksi väriä yhdessä' — vague and faintly celebratory; 'päällekkäin' states literally that one landed on the other.
